book.title: The Information Studies Degree Planner
book.subtitle: Department of Information Studies, East West University
lines: Twenty-six core courses from information literacy to Linux servers. A planner for the two skills this degree is hired for: organising knowledge and building the systems that hold it.
small: Curriculum, rules, fees and dates checked against East West University's official web pages on 10 October 2026.

Unofficial. An independent planner for students. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or issued by East West University. Always confirm requirements with your advisor, the student portal and official notices.

book.text: This planner puts your whole Information Studies degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.

items: **Degree** - the BSS in Information Studies as EWU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on EWU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - EWU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.
It is **not an official EWU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from EWU's own web pages on 10 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.
On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from East West University's published pages as they stood on 10 October 2026; the source is named under each section.
A+ to D are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA.

items: **An F stays in the sum.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top, until you retake the course and the old F becomes an R.
**Heavier courses move the CGPA more.** A 4-credit course with a lab outweighs a 3-credit one. Protect the heavy courses first.
**W, I, P and S never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

items: You may retake a course **only once** to improve a grade you already earned.

A retake needs the **Department Chair's written permission** and full tuition, lab and other fees.

book.title: Before you retake a passing grade
items: Run the numbers in the CGPA tab's retake what-if. A B- to A- retake on a 3-credit course lifts 2.25 quality points - on 90 GPA credits that is 0.025 of CGPA. Decide whether that is worth a full course fee and your scholarship eligibility.

rows: CGPA from 1.00 to below 2.25 after your first two semesters, or any later one, puts you on probation for the next two semesters. Reach 2.25 by then or be dismissed. On probation you cannot drop a semester or take leave.
CGPA below 1.00 after the first two or any later semester means automatic dismissal. A dismissed student may apply to another program by passing its admission test.
The academic calendar sets an in-person advising day for students with CGPA 2.15 or less (admitted up to Summer 2023) or 2.40 or less (admitted from Fall 2023), and for everyone on probation.

A student in good standing can take up to three consecutive semesters (one academic year) of leave through the Dean, naming the return semester. Absence without permission is penalised - 20%, 30% or 40% of nine credits' tuition for one, two or three semesters - and beyond three semesters you are withdrawn.
The student rules ask for attendance of not less than 70%-80% of lectures, tutorials and practical classes in each course. Check each course outline for the figure your instructor applies.

Final scripts are not re-evaluated. You can ask for a check of marking or totalling errors for Tk 200 a script (refunded if the error was the faculty member's). Grade changes must reach the Controller of Examinations within seven days of the next semester.

Zero tolerance for copying, unauthorised help and other unfair means; cases go to the Dean. EWU also publishes a Plagiarism Policy and an Artificial Intelligence Policy (ewubd.edu/ewu-policies) - read both before you submit work made with any tool.

book.text: the Toolkit tab - The Information Studies toolkit

Half of this degree is about describing things so precisely that anyone can find them; the other half is about building the systems that do the finding. Seven tools: three for describing and finding, two for building, and two for choosing where you go next.
Classification is learned by volume. Do ten items a week in the scheme and edition your course teaches, and write down *why* each number is what it is - the reasoning is what is marked.

columns.h: How I built it (base number, tables, notes)

items: What is the item **about** - not what is its title?
Is there **one subject, several subjects, or one subject from a viewpoint**?
Which **discipline** is it written for?
Is there a **place, period or form** that the scheme lets me add?
Would a user looking for this subject **find it here**?
